title.narrative: Coordination of public/private partnership and promoting access to universal birth registration in Côte d’Ivoire

description.narrative: Lack of birth registration tends to negatively impact child labour prevalence. Children without legal identity are more at risk of becoming victims of trafficking and/or child labour than children that have their births registered. While access to school is guaranteed to all children, passing from primary to secondary school requires a birth certificate which leaves many children out of school. Out of school children are at particular risk of becoming victims of child labour without proper education opportunities for professional training and apprentice. Furthermore, children who are victims of trafficking are often without legal identity and nationality thereby at greater risk for illegal work and child labour.Although major progress has been made, 32% of children younger than one year old are still not registered (Côte d’Ivoire Annual Vital Statistics Report, 2021) and the cocoa growing regions in Côte d’Ivoire have some of the lowest birth registration rates. In order to accelerate progress in birth registration and ensure that every child has a legal identity, UNICEF Côte d’Ivoire is supporting the Government of Côte d’Ivoire in three key areas of intervention:1. Scaling-up interoperability with the health sector by integrating civil registration into routine health processes as a cost-effective manner to increase birth registration rate; 2. Operationalizing the Special Law allowing for late registration of children free of charge for systematic registration of children who do not have a birth certificate; and3. Facilitating and strengthening public-private collaboration between private companies, targeting primarily the cocoa sector, and the Government to jointly address the issue of (late) birth registration as well as direct efforts towards civil registration system strengthening for more sustained actions.These activities will be implemented in a target cocoa-producing region in order to test and document the results achieved with a view to future scaling up in other regions of Côte d’Ivoire.The project will help strengthen the position of Côte d’Ivoire as a pioneer champion country for birth registration and will contribute to the fight against child labour in the cocoa sector. In this pilot government actors of Cote d'Ivoire and private sector actors will join forces to increase birth registration in cocoa producing regions.
